NVAX: # Novavax (NVAX) — research brief **As of 16 October 2026. Focus ticker only.** ## What the company is Novavax is a vaccine company. Its revenue now leans on partners who sell the product, plus milestone and royalty payments, rather than on large direct product sales of its own ([Novavax (NVAX) Surge, Early October 2026](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-novavax-nvax-stock-up-20-65-today-17829/)). A partnership payment changes cash and risk; it does not change commercial performance. ## The price move As of 15 October 2026 20:50 UTC, NVAX was up 14.3% over one week, 28.3% over one month and 62.6% over three months, and 1.3% on the day. Over five years it is down 92.3% (Market Explorer observation). A Zopedia snapshot at 9 October 2026 04:00 UTC put the close at $12.745. The 5-day return was +21.7%, the 21-day +36.9%, the 63-day +43.0%. The 14-day RSI was 68.1, near the 70 level that often marks an overbought market. The 20-day annualised volatility was 95%. Price sat about 90% up its recent channel, with resistance at $13.385 and support at $7.15 ([NVAX — Novavax](https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/NVAX/)). In the week of 5–7 October 2026, NVAX rose about 20%. Reports show a close of $12.56 on 5 October, up 20.08% on about 28.5 million shares; an intraday print of $12.12, up 15.9%, as a new 52-week high; and a print of $12.62, up 20.65%, about $2.16 above a prior close of $10.46. All three imply a prior close near $10.46, so they probably describe the same session at different times. One source shows an $11.01 close for 8 October, which does not agree with the $12.745 snapshot. The daily close series for 1–9 October 2026 is not settled ([Novavax (NVAX) Surge, Early October 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-novavax-stock-surging-today-93CH-4932717)). ## Reported drivers Three causes are reported, not confirmed: - **An FDA-related catalyst.** An opened FDA page lists Nuvaxovid as approved, but the page is archived with an 08 July 2026 expiry. It does not confirm a new October 2026 action. - **A Sanofi agreement**, reported as a $500 million upfront payment, up to $700 million in future milestones, and royalties on future sales. This is the single most important number in the file. The exact terms, the 2026 triggers and the timing are not confirmed. - **Vaccine-sector strength.** Benzinga reported on 9–10 October 2026 that a new NIH-backed initiative to speed up personalised cancer vaccine development sent MRNA, BNTX and NVAX higher; live evidence says the NIH plans a public-private cancer vaccine programme starting in December, focused on pancreatic and liver cancer ([A New War on Cancer?](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally), [Vaccine Stocks Rally](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/vaccine-stocks-rally-reports-u-141200740.html)). On the same day, 24/7 Wall St reported NVAX at $12.77, up 16% (its own quick-read block said 14%), MRNA at $219.30, up 11%, MRK at $146.18, up 3%, the iShares Biotechnology ETF up 3% and SPY up 0.5% ([24/7 Wall St via AOL](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally)). ## What the company's own numbers show Period 2026Q1 (report date 31 March 2026): - Revenue $139.5 million, down 79.1% from a year earlier. The year-earlier quarter was far larger, and this revenue line is lumpy because it depends on partner payments and seasonal vaccine sales. - Net income -$9.5 million, against -$202.4 million in 2025Q3. - Operating cash flow -$32.4 million. - Free cash flow +$6.1 million, the first positive reading since 2025Q3. - Stockholders' equity -$144.8 million. - Total assets $1,043.2 million; total liabilities $1,187.9 million. Negative stockholders' equity has been the normal state since late 2021, with only brief positive readings. Liabilities have exceeded assets over the same period. Negative equity is a chronic condition, not a new one. ## Bull hypothesis **Mechanism.** Novavax has shifted from paying for its own manufacturing and sales to collecting partner payments. If the Sanofi agreement delivers a $500 million upfront, up to $700 million in milestones and a royalty stream, that cash arrives without a matching cost, which extends runway and makes revenue less dependent on the company's own commercial spending. At the same time, the net loss has narrowed sharply and free cash flow turned positive in 2026Q1. A group-level vaccine rally lifts the whole sector, and NVAX is a high-volatility member of it. **Supporting facts.** Price momentum is verified: +14.3% / +28.3% / +62.6% over one week, one month and three months. Sector news is dated and sourced. The reported Sanofi amounts are specific. The 2026Q1 free-cash-flow turn and the narrower loss are in the supplied financials. Health Care led sectors on 15 October 2026. **Assumptions.** The reported Sanofi terms are real and paid on the described timetable. The October FDA item is a genuine new action, not a re-reading of an older approval. Novavax has a real role in the NIH programme, not just a sympathy bid. **Counterevidence.** The October catalysts are reported, not confirmed. The archived FDA page does not confirm a new action. No source shows Novavax as a participant in the NIH programme. Revenue still fell sharply and equity is negative. RSI at 68.1 and price 90% up the channel mean the move is extended. **Invalidation.** The bull case breaks if the Sanofi upfront or milestones are not confirmed and paid; if the October FDA action turns out to be a re-report of an older approval; if price falls back below the $10.46 prior close; if the NIH programme names participants and Novavax is not among them; or if the next filing shows free cash flow back in negative territory. ## Bear hypothesis **Mechanism.** The rally is a headline-and-sympathy move in a company whose commercial position has shrunk. Revenue is small and lumpy, and the balance sheet carries negative equity. Any financing — equity issuance or convertible debt — would dilute existing holders, in a stock that already lost 92.3% over five years. Subsiding momentum in a 95%-volatility name can reverse quickly, and a cancer-vaccine headline does not transfer unless the company has a cancer-vaccine product. **Supporting facts.** Five-year return -92.3%. 2026Q1 revenue $139.5 million, down 79.1% year over year. Operating cash flow -$32.4 million. Stockholders' equity -$144.8 million. Liabilities ($1,187.9 million) exceed assets ($1,043.2 million). Annualised volatility 95%. RSI 68.1. No analyst data, share count, cash balance or free float was retrieved. **Assumptions.** Partner and royalty payments are not enough to fund the business at its current cost level. The sector rally fades. No new company-specific positive event arrives. **Counterevidence.** A large, low-cost Sanofi cash inflow is exactly what the bear case must explain away. The 2026Q1 free-cash-flow turn and the narrower loss are early evidence against a permanent cash-burn view. The group bid from the NIH headline was real on the day, and Health Care led sectors on 15 October 2026. **Invalidation.** The bear case breaks if the Sanofi payment is confirmed and received; if the next filing shows growth in partner and royalty revenue; if free cash flow stays positive for a second quarter; if the company raises cash without issuing equity; or if short-interest data shows the rally was a squeeze that has now cleared. ## Which thesis the facts favour Over one week to one month, the facts favour the bull case on momentum and sector direction, because those two things are verified and point the same way. The edge is thin, not strong: the company-specific catalysts are reported rather than confirmed, and the price is extended inside its channel. Over three months, the question is whether the Sanofi money and the 2026–2027 COVID season actually land. This file does not settle that. The 2026Q1 free-cash-flow turn is the only company-specific datapoint pointing bullish; the revenue fall and negative equity point the other way. Neither side has a supportable edge at that horizon from this evidence. Over five years, the record is clearly negative at -92.3%, and nothing in this file shows a product that reverses it. I would not claim a bullish edge at that horizon. ## Facts to obtain next - The Sanofi agreement's exact upfront amount, milestone schedule, royalty rate and 2026 triggers. - The exact FDA action behind the 5–6 October 2026 move, and whether Nuvaxovid's approval was renewed or extended after 8 July 2026. - The current cash and short-term investments balance, share count, and any at-the-market or other financing. - Whether Novavax is named in the NIH personalised cancer vaccine programme. - Analyst estimate revisions and price targets after 9 October 2026. - Short interest and free float, to test whether a squeeze produced the move. - A reconciled daily close series for 1–9 October 2026.

CORZ: **Answer: For one week and one month, neither the bull nor the bear case has a clean edge. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, but the bull case is not disproved. The decisive year-ahead question is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases.** **Company identity.** Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) is a bitcoin miner that now sells high-density data-center space. That business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI and high-performance computing customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024. CoreWeave agreed to acquire Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (CoreWeave to acquire Core Scientific, company press release). That deal did not complete. A retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination timing as unverified. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ. **Price move.** On 15 October 2026, CORZ rose 7.1% on the day. But it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months, and -27.5% over one year. The day's gain came against a falling semiconductor and AI-hardware tape driven by rate-hike fears (Rate Pressure vs. AI Demand: Rising Treasury Yields Trigger Nvidia, AMD Slump). Similar single-day gains in Cipher and TeraWulf look like a catalyst-free oversold bounce. Treat 15 October as group mean-reversion in beaten-down miner and data-center names until a company-specific driver appears. Do not use the 7-8 October price points in the retained snippets: one says CORZ fell 4.4% to $15.94 on 2026-10-07, another says it closed down 3.67% at $18.10 on 2026-10-08. These cannot both be right, so no price level should be taken from them. **Shared driver, not company failure.** The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders. On 7-8 October, Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose ([IREN Falls 7% as Financing-Heavy Data Center Names Sell Off Apart From Their Sector Fund; TeraWulf and Core Scientific Drop 5%](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/07/iren-falls-7-as-financing-heavy-data-center-names-sell-off-apart-from-their-sector-fund-terawulf-and-core-scientific-drop-5)). Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate ([CoreWeave Stock Keeps Sinking As Wall Street Questions Its Debt-Fueled AI Empire](https://benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62378700/coreweave-stock-keeps-sinking-as-wall-street-questions-its-debt-fueled-ai-empire)) and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. This matters because Core Scientific must borrow to build. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion ([Capital Over Chips: Broadcom CEO Warns Financing Costs Could Slow AI Expansion](https://benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/10/62379402/capital-over-chips-broadcom-ceo-warns-financing-costs-could-slow-ai-expansion)). **Reported results for the quarter ended 2026-06-30.** Revenue was $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M a year earlier. Operating income was +$20.7M. Gross profit was $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA was $41.1M. Liquidity was $1.82B ([Core Scientific Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results](https://investors.corescientific.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/139/core-scientific-announces-second-quarter-2026-results)). The build-out is the dominant financial fact: total assets rose to $5.26B from $3.07B at 31 March 2026, and total liabilities rose to $7.68B from $4.38B. **Read the cash flow correctly.** Free cash flow was -$1.02B in Q2 2026. This is a quarterly figure. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Most of the -$1.02B is capital spending, because operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive. The funding need is growth investment, not operating losses. That single quarter's outflow is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025. The money comes from outside the business: a $3.3B 7.75% senior secured notes offering described in the Q1 2026 release ([Core Scientific Announces First Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Results](https://investors.corescientific.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/136/core-scientific-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-results)); $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities reported 14 September 2026 ([Core Scientific (CORZ) lines up fresh credit to free cash for AI infrastructure](https://stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CORZ/8-k-core-scientific-inc-tx-reports-material-event-a86a4bdfb955.html)); and conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas sites on 14 September 2026 ([Core Scientific wins conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data centers](https://tradingview.com/news/tradingview:b55357bd92728:0-core-scientific-wins-conditional-ercot-power-approvals-for-texas-data-centers)). ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions. **Negative equity.** Stockholders' equity was -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are greater than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event. Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026. That swing points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss. The binding constraints are liquidity and continued access to debt and equity on acceptable terms. **Bull case, mechanism and support.** Core Scientific owns low-cost power and land. Converting it to high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt and per dollar invested once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin. On 28 July 2026, the company announced an AMD partnership covering 500+ MW of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW. MW means megawatt, a unit of power. GW means gigawatt, 1,000 megawatts. ERCOT conditional approvals support the Texas pipeline. Assumption: the pipeline becomes signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt. Invalidation: announcements do not turn into contracts with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates; or leasing rents and utilization fall short of the cost of capital. **Bear case, mechanism and support.** A capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads, or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow, $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets, negative equity, and demonstrated sensitivity to financing news. Counterevidence that weakens it: the recent fall is sector- and rate-driven rather than a CORZ-specific operating failure. The only company-specific October item in the evidence is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05: Investing.com India: Core Scientific Officer Todd Duchene Sells $163,055 in Stock). That sale is too small to explain the decline. **Verdict by horizon.** For one week and one month, neither side has a clean edge. The direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates, which the company does not control. Note that Q2 2026 results were reported on 28 July 2026, so a Q3 2026 report is likely within the one-month window, even though the confirmed date is not in the evidence. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The decisive variable over a year is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases. **What to obtain next.** The CoreWeave deal termination date. Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates. The Q3 2026 report date and results. The leasing rents and utilization for the new high-density halls compared with the cost of the new debt.

CRGY: **Bottom line: the facts identify the catalyst and the mechanics clearly, but they do not yet support a directional edge for either side over the next week, month or quarter. The decisive numbers — what Crescent paid per unit of production, how the purchase was funded, and what the combined company earns per share — are not in the evidence.** **What the company is, and what just happened** Crescent Energy Company Class A common stock (ticker CRGY, SEC filer number CIK 1866175) is an independent oil and gas producer with assets in the Permian and Eagle Ford areas. It grows mainly by buying other producers rather than by drilling new ground. It was formed in 2021 by combining Contango Oil & Gas with KKR-backed Independence Energy, and it closed the purchase of Vital Energy's Permian assets on 2025-12-15 for about $3.1 billion including net debt, which the company described as accretive ([CRGY - Crescent Energy Company Class A Common Stock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm)). The current event is the same pattern, larger. On 2026-10-08, Devon Energy agreed to sell its Eagle Ford assets to Crescent for about $4.2 billion in cash, covering roughly 90,000 net acres; one report gives the purchase value as about $3.85 billion and cites roughly $140 million of annual cost savings ([Crescent Energy buys Devon Energy Eagle Ford assets for $4.2B and prices $1B equity offering (October 2026)](https://www.benzinga.com/m/26/10/62241109/devon-energy-sell-its-eagle-ford-assets-crescent-energy-4-2b-cash), [CRGY October 2026 Devon Eagle Ford purchase and Class A stock offering](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRGY/8-k-crescent-energy-company-reports-material-event-0a498471893d.html)). The same day the company started a $1 billion offering of Class A shares. It priced on 2026-10-09 at $12.50 a share for 80 million shares, and a KKR affiliate agreed to buy 40 million of them ([Crescent Energy $1B Class A common stock offering (2026-10-08)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm), [StockTitan: Crescent Energy prices 80M-share stock offering at $12.50](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRGY/8-k-crescent-energy-company-reports-material-event-0a498471893d.html)). One retained record links the offering proceeds to funding the Devon purchase. Another record says the reports do not state the use of proceeds or whether the 80 million shares are new shares, existing shares sold by holders, or a mix. **Reported results before the deal.** For the quarter that ended 2026-06-30, the supplied data show revenue of about $1.39 billion, net income of about $493 million and operating cash flow, the cash a business produces from normal operations, of about $944 million. Total assets were about $12.0 billion, total liabilities about $6.85 billion and shareholders' equity about $5.16 billion. The prior quarter, which ended 2026-03-31, showed a net loss of about $420 million on revenue of about $1.18 billion. The record does not explain what drove the swing between the two quarters. **The bullish hypothesis.** Mechanism: a repeat buyer of oil and gas assets gains scale in the Eagle Ford at a price that is cheaper than building the same production, and the reported cost savings lower the combined unit cost. Supporting facts: the consolidator model has a recent completed example (the Vital Energy Permian purchase, closed 2025-12-15), the $1 billion equity raise removes the need to fund the full cash price from the balance sheet alone, a KKR affiliate committed to half of the offered shares, and second-quarter 2026 results were strongly cash generative. Assumption: the acquisition earns more than its cost of capital and the equity issuance is small relative to the added cash flow. Counterevidence: no purchase agreement terms, no acquired production or reserve figures, no close date and no pro forma financials are in the evidence, so the claim that the deal is accretive cannot be tested. Invalidation: disclosure showing the purchase price per unit of production above comparable regional deals, or pro forma debt that is higher than before the deal without a path to reduce it. **The bearish hypothesis.** Mechanism: the company pays $4.2 billion in cash and sells 80 million new shares at $12.50 to help fund it, so each existing share now represents a smaller slice of the business and more debt. The stock has traded near the offering price since pricing: it closed at $12.84 on 2026-10-14 and fell 2.65% on 2026-10-15 ([CRGY - Crescent Energy Company Class A Common Stock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm)). Supporting facts: the 1-month return is -11.38% and the 1-week return is -7.20% as of 2026-10-15, and the deal report falls inside the 1-week window. Counterevidence: the 3-month return is +20.66%, so the shares are still well above where they started the quarter, and the 1-month window began around 2026-09-14, before the deal was announced, so the deal cannot explain the whole decline. Invalidation: a firm financing plan that holds pro forma debt near current levels, or evidence that per-share cash flow rises after the deal closes. **Which thesis the facts favor.** Neither has a clear edge. The decline is concentrated around a share sale and a large cash purchase, which is consistent with the bearish mechanism, but the same facts are equally consistent with a market that simply repriced the new share count. The bullish mechanism depends on deal economics that are not disclosed. Company identity is confirmed, the catalyst is dated and described, and the pre-deal results are solid on cash generation. Beyond that, the evidence does not settle the question, and guessing would be inventing an edge. **By horizon.** - **1 week:** driven by how the market absorbs the 80 million new shares and whether the stock holds near $12.50. No edge from the evidence. - **1 month:** driven by any further detail on funding, closing conditions and third-quarter results for the period ended 2026-09-30. No edge until those appear. - **3 month:** driven by whether the acquired assets add cash flow per share and whether debt falls. The 3-month return of +20.66% shows the market rewarded the equity earlier in this period, so the pullback is a partial give-back, not a full reversal. **Facts to obtain next.** The purchase agreement: total consideration, cash versus stock, debt financing, expected close date and conditions. The acquired production, reserves and cash flow, so the price can be compared with other Eagle Ford and Permian deals. Pro forma debt, earnings and per-share cash flow, plus share count before and after the offering. Whether the 80 million shares are newly issued. And the driver of the swing from the 2026-03-31 net loss to the 2026-06-30 net profit, including hedging and one-off items.

Revenue growing while the loss widens means cost growth is running ahead of pricing. On credit, S&P Global Ratings lowered JetBlue to CCC+ from B- on 8 June 2026 with a stable outlook, citing elevated fuel costs and sustained high leverage ([JetBlue Financials: Losses, Debt & JetForward Turnaround](https://dwuconsulting.com/dwu-ai/jetblue-airways-financial-profile)). CCC+ is a rating grade that signals substantial credit risk. A separate CreditSights note frames cash burn and Middle East tensions as the drivers of liquidity concern, with financing options drawing focus ([JetBlue cash burn, Middle East tensions fuel liquidity concerns](https://know.creditsights.com/insights/us-special-situations-jetblue-cash-burn-middle-east-tensions-fuel-liquidity-concerns-as-financing-options-draw-focus/)). ## Bearish hypothesis **Mechanism:** Fuel, labour and airport costs rise faster than the money collected per seat mile. Revenue per seat grows, but the loss widens anyway, so the company keeps spending more cash than it earns. Falling equity and high leverage then make borrowing more expensive or force a share sale, which spreads the same profit over more shares. **Supporting facts:** Q2 2026 revenue up 14.5% but the loss about three times wider; negative free cash flow in every quarter shown; equity down about 40% from 2024Q4; the S&P downgrade to CCC+; negative analyst target revisions into 14 October 2026. **Assumption:** The cost trend of the last reported quarter continues into the third quarter. **Counterevidence:** Susquehanna kept a Neutral rating rather than Sell, and the 13 October commentary described the situation as a contrarian setup. Revenue and unit revenue did grow. **Observable invalidation:** The Q3 2026 report shows a narrower loss and unit revenue growth above unit cost growth; or no new financing is needed on expensive terms; or a credit rater lifts the outlook. ## Bullish hypothesis **Mechanism:** The JetForward turnaround pushes revenue up faster than costs. Higher revenue per seat then converts into a smaller loss rather than a wider one, and a stock near its 52-week low with a Sell rating already priced in re-rates when the loss narrows. **Supporting facts:** Revenue rose 14.5% year on year in 2026Q2 and unit revenue grew; the shares bounced 4.66% on 15 October 2026. **Assumption:** Fuel prices fall or capacity is cut enough that cost growth slows below revenue growth. **Counterevidence:** The loss widened in the same quarter that revenue grew, which is the opposite of the mechanism. Goldman Sachs carries a Sell rating, and S&P rates the debt CCC+. One up day inside a 42% three-month fall does not show a change in the business. **Observable invalidation:** The Q3 2026 report shows a further widening loss, or a new share issue or expensive borrowing, or another credit downgrade. ## Which thesis the facts favour The bearish thesis has the better support on the facts in hand, because the only reported quarter shows costs outrunning pricing while cash leaves the business, and because the credit and analyst moves point the same way. That is an edge on the reported trajectory, not a forecast. The bullish case rests on a turnaround that has not yet appeared in any reported number, so it is a claim about the future rather than a reading of the evidence. The edge is strongest over one week to three months and weakest over one year to five years, where the outcome depends on whether the turnaround ever produces positive free cash flow. That question is unresolved. ## Facts to obtain next - The third-quarter 2026 results, due on the call at 10:00 a.m. ET on 27 October 2026 (JetBlue Announces Webcast of Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call, 13 October 2026). Unit revenue against unit cost is the decisive comparison. - The company's stated full-year 2026 guidance and any capacity or route changes. - Total liquidity and the maturity schedule for the next twelve months, to test how far cash burn can continue without new funding. - The fuel hedge position and the current share count. - Whether the 13 and 14 October 2026 price falls had a company-specific trigger beyond the analyst revisions. This is research, not a recommendation to buy or sell.

# CORZ — Core Scientific, Inc. Common Stock

## Identity
Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) mines bitcoin and rents high-density data-center space. The rental business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI (artificial intelligence) and HPC (high-performance computing) customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024.

## Merger history (one conflicting date)
CoreWeave agreed to buy Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (company press release). That deal did not complete. One retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination date as unverified until a filing or press release confirms it. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ.

## Reported results, quarter ended 30 June 2026
- Revenue: $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M one year earlier.
- Operating income: +$20.7M. Gross profit: $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA: $41.1M. Liquidity: $1.82B.
- Total assets: $5.26B, up from $3.07B at 31 March 2026. Total liabilities: $7.68B, up from $4.38B.
- Stockholders' equity: -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are larger than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event.
- Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026, which points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss.

## Cash flow
The free cash flow figure was -$1.02B in Q2 2026, and this is a quarterly number. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive, so most of the outflow is capital spending. That one quarter is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025.

## Funding and pipeline
- $3.3B of 7.75% senior secured notes, described in the Q1 2026 results release.
- $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities, reported 14 September 2026.
- Conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data-center sites, reported 14 September 2026. ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions.
- AMD partnership announced 28 July 2026: 500+ MW (megawatts, a unit of power) of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW (gigawatts, 1,000 megawatts).

## Price action and its driver
On 15 October 2026 CORZ rose 7.1% on the day, but it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months and -27.5% over one year. Two retained price points for 7-8 October conflict: one reports a $15.94 price on 2026-10-07 and another reports a close of $18.10 on 2026-10-08. Neither should be used.

The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders, not a CORZ-specific operating failure. On 7-8 October 2026 Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose. Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion. The only company-specific October item found is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05), which is too small to explain the decline.

## Competing forward-looking theses as of 15 October 2026
Bull case: converting low-cost power and land into high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin, and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The assumption to test is that announcements become signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt.

Bear case: a capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow; $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets; negative equity.

Neither side has a clean edge at one week or one month, because direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates. At three months and one year the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating.

## Facts to obtain next
- The CoreWeave deal termination date.
- Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity, with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates.
- The Q3 2026 report date and results.
- Leasing rents and utilization for the new high-density halls compared with the cost of the new debt.

ticker_packages.answer_markdown: # Novavax (NVAX) — research brief **As of 16 October 2026. Focus ticker only.** ## What the company is Novavax is a vaccine company. Its revenue now leans on partners who sell the product, plus milestone and royalty payments, rather than on large direct product sales of its own ([Novavax (NVAX) Surge, Early October 2026](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-novavax-nvax-stock-up-20-65-today-17829/)). A partnership payment changes cash and risk; it does not change commercial performance. ## The price move As of 15 October 2026 20:50 UTC, NVAX was up 14.3% over one week, 28.3% over one month and 62.6% over three months, and 1.3% on the day. Over five years it is down 92.3% (Market Explorer observation). A Zopedia snapshot at 9 October 2026 04:00 UTC put the close at $12.745. The 5-day return was +21.7%, the 21-day +36.9%, the 63-day +43.0%. The 14-day RSI was 68.1, near the 70 level that often marks an overbought market. The 20-day annualised volatility was 95%. Price sat about 90% up its recent channel, with resistance at $13.385 and support at $7.15 ([NVAX — Novavax](https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/NVAX/)). In the week of 5–7 October 2026, NVAX rose about 20%. Reports show a close of $12.56 on 5 October, up 20.08% on about 28.5 million shares; an intraday print of $12.12, up 15.9%, as a new 52-week high; and a print of $12.62, up 20.65%, about $2.16 above a prior close of $10.46. All three imply a prior close near $10.46, so they probably describe the same session at different times. One source shows an $11.01 close for 8 October, which does not agree with the $12.745 snapshot. The daily close series for 1–9 October 2026 is not settled ([Novavax (NVAX) Surge, Early October 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-novavax-stock-surging-today-93CH-4932717)). ## Reported drivers Three causes are reported, not confirmed: - **An FDA-related catalyst.** An opened FDA page lists Nuvaxovid as approved, but the page is archived with an 08 July 2026 expiry. It does not confirm a new October 2026 action. - **A Sanofi agreement**, reported as a $500 million upfront payment, up to $700 million in future milestones, and royalties on future sales. This is the single most important number in the file. The exact terms, the 2026 triggers and the timing are not confirmed. - **Vaccine-sector strength.** Benzinga reported on 9–10 October 2026 that a new NIH-backed initiative to speed up personalised cancer vaccine development sent MRNA, BNTX and NVAX higher; live evidence says the NIH plans a public-private cancer vaccine programme starting in December, focused on pancreatic and liver cancer ([A New War on Cancer?](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally), [Vaccine Stocks Rally](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/vaccine-stocks-rally-reports-u-141200740.html)). On the same day, 24/7 Wall St reported NVAX at $12.77, up 16% (its own quick-read block said 14%), MRNA at $219.30, up 11%, MRK at $146.18, up 3%, the iShares Biotechnology ETF up 3% and SPY up 0.5% ([24/7 Wall St via AOL](https://benzinga.com/news/health-care/26/10/62283036/a-new-war-on-cancer-nihs-vaccine-initiative-sparks-biotech-stock-rally)). ## What the company's own numbers show Period 2026Q1 (report date 31 March 2026): - Revenue $139.5 million, down 79.1% from a year earlier. The year-earlier quarter was far larger, and this revenue line is lumpy because it depends on partner payments and seasonal vaccine sales. - Net income -$9.5 million, against -$202.4 million in 2025Q3. - Operating cash flow -$32.4 million. - Free cash flow +$6.1 million, the first positive reading since 2025Q3. - Stockholders' equity -$144.8 million. - Total assets $1,043.2 million; total liabilities $1,187.9 million. Negative stockholders' equity has been the normal state since late 2021, with only brief positive readings. Liabilities have exceeded assets over the same period. Negative equity is a chronic condition, not a new one. ## Bull hypothesis **Mechanism.** Novavax has shifted from paying for its own manufacturing and sales to collecting partner payments. If the Sanofi agreement delivers a $500 million upfront, up to $700 million in milestones and a royalty stream, that cash arrives without a matching cost, which extends runway and makes revenue less dependent on the company's own commercial spending. At the same time, the net loss has narrowed sharply and free cash flow turned positive in 2026Q1. A group-level vaccine rally lifts the whole sector, and NVAX is a high-volatility member of it. **Supporting facts.** Price momentum is verified: +14.3% / +28.3% / +62.6% over one week, one month and three months. Sector news is dated and sourced. The reported Sanofi amounts are specific. The 2026Q1 free-cash-flow turn and the narrower loss are in the supplied financials. Health Care led sectors on 15 October 2026. **Assumptions.** The reported Sanofi terms are real and paid on the described timetable. The October FDA item is a genuine new action, not a re-reading of an older approval. Novavax has a real role in the NIH programme, not just a sympathy bid. **Counterevidence.** The October catalysts are reported, not confirmed. The archived FDA page does not confirm a new action. No source shows Novavax as a participant in the NIH programme. Revenue still fell sharply and equity is negative. RSI at 68.1 and price 90% up the channel mean the move is extended. **Invalidation.** The bull case breaks if the Sanofi upfront or milestones are not confirmed and paid; if the October FDA action turns out to be a re-report of an older approval; if price falls back below the $10.46 prior close; if the NIH programme names participants and Novavax is not among them; or if the next filing shows free cash flow back in negative territory. ## Bear hypothesis **Mechanism.** The rally is a headline-and-sympathy move in a company whose commercial position has shrunk. Revenue is small and lumpy, and the balance sheet carries negative equity. Any financing — equity issuance or convertible debt — would dilute existing holders, in a stock that already lost 92.3% over five years. ticker_packages.answer_markdown: **Answer: For one week and one month, neither the bull nor the bear case has a clean edge. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, but the bull case is not disproved. The decisive year-ahead question is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases.** **Company identity.** Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) is a bitcoin miner that now sells high-density data-center space. That business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI and high-performance computing customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024. CoreWeave agreed to acquire Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (CoreWeave to acquire Core Scientific, company press release). That deal did not complete. A retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination timing as unverified. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ. **Price move.** On 15 October 2026, CORZ rose 7.1% on the day. But it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months, and -27.5% over one year. The day's gain came against a falling semiconductor and AI-hardware tape driven by rate-hike fears (Rate Pressure vs. AI Demand: Rising Treasury Yields Trigger Nvidia, AMD Slump). Similar single-day gains in Cipher and TeraWulf look like a catalyst-free oversold bounce. Treat 15 October as group mean-reversion in beaten-down miner and data-center names until a company-specific driver appears. Do not use the 7-8 October price points in the retained snippets: one says CORZ fell 4.4% to $15.94 on 2026-10-07, another says it closed down 3.67% at $18.10 on 2026-10-08. These cannot both be right, so no price level should be taken from them. **Shared driver, not company failure.** The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders. On 7-8 October, Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose ([IREN Falls 7% as Financing-Heavy Data Center Names Sell Off Apart From Their Sector Fund; TeraWulf and Core Scientific Drop 5%](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/07/iren-falls-7-as-financing-heavy-data-center-names-sell-off-apart-from-their-sector-fund-terawulf-and-core-scientific-drop-5)). Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate ([CoreWeave Stock Keeps Sinking As Wall Street Questions Its Debt-Fueled AI Empire](https://benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62378700/coreweave-stock-keeps-sinking-as-wall-street-questions-its-debt-fueled-ai-empire)) and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. This matters because Core Scientific must borrow to build. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion ([Capital Over Chips: Broadcom CEO Warns Financing Costs Could Slow AI Expansion](https://benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/10/62379402/capital-over-chips-broadcom-ceo-warns-financing-costs-could-slow-ai-expansion)). **Reported results for the quarter ended 2026-06-30.** Revenue was $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M a year earlier. Operating income was +$20.7M. Gross profit was $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA was $41.1M. Liquidity was $1.82B ([Core Scientific Announces Second Quarter 2026 Results](https://investors.corescientific.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/139/core-scientific-announces-second-quarter-2026-results)). The build-out is the dominant financial fact: total assets rose to $5.26B from $3.07B at 31 March 2026, and total liabilities rose to $7.68B from $4.38B. **Read the cash flow correctly.** Free cash flow was -$1.02B in Q2 2026. This is a quarterly figure. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Most of the -$1.02B is capital spending, because operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive. The funding need is growth investment, not operating losses. That single quarter's outflow is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025. The money comes from outside the business: a $3.3B 7.75% senior secured notes offering described in the Q1 2026 release ([Core Scientific Announces First Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Results](https://investors.corescientific.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/136/core-scientific-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-results)); $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities reported 14 September 2026 ([Core Scientific (CORZ) lines up fresh credit to free cash for AI infrastructure](https://stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CORZ/8-k-core-scientific-inc-tx-reports-material-event-a86a4bdfb955.html)); and conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas sites on 14 September 2026 ([Core Scientific wins conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data centers](https://tradingview.com/news/tradingview:b55357bd92728:0-core-scientific-wins-conditional-ercot-power-approvals-for-texas-data-centers)). ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions. **Negative equity.** Stockholders' equity was -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are greater than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event. Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026. That swing points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss. The binding constraints are liquidity and continued access to debt and equity on acceptable terms. **Bull case, mechanism and support.** Core Scientific owns low-cost power and land. Converting it to high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt and per dollar invested once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin. On 28 July 2026, the company announced an AMD partnership covering 500+ MW of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW. MW means megawatt, a unit of power. GW means gigawatt, 1,000 megawatts. ERCOT conditional approvals support the Texas pipeline. Assumption: the pipeline becomes signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt. Invalidation: announcements do not turn into contracts with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates; or leasing rents and utilization fall short of the cost of capital. **Bear case, mechanism and support.** A capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads, or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow, $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets, negative equity, and demonstrated sensitivity to financing news. Counterevidence that weakens it: the recent fall is sector- and rate-driven rather than a CORZ-specific operating failure. The only company-specific October item in the evidence is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05: Investing.com India: Core Scientific Officer Todd Duchene Sells $163,055 in Stock). That sale is too small to explain the decline. **Verdict by horizon.** For one week and one month, neither side has a clean edge. The direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates, which the company does not control. Note that Q2 2026 results were reported on 28 July 2026, so a Q3 2026 report is likely within the one-month window, even though the confirmed date is not in the evidence. For three months and one year, the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The decisive variable over a year is whether announced capacity becomes signed, funded leases. **What to obtain next.** The CoreWeave deal termination date. Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates. The Q3 2026 report date and results. The leasing rents and utilization for the new high-density halls compared with the cost of the new debt.

## Identity
Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) mines bitcoin and rents high-density data-center space. The rental business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI (artificial intelligence) and HPC (high-performance computing) customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024.

## Merger history (one conflicting date)
CoreWeave agreed to buy Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (company press release). That deal did not complete. One retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination date as unverified until a filing or press release confirms it. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ.

## Reported results, quarter ended 30 June 2026
- Revenue: $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M one year earlier.
- Operating income: +$20.7M. Gross profit: $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA: $41.1M. Liquidity: $1.82B.
- Total assets: $5.26B, up from $3.07B at 31 March 2026. Total liabilities: $7.68B, up from $4.38B.
- Stockholders' equity: -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are larger than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event.
- Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026, which points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss.

## Cash flow
The free cash flow figure was -$1.02B in Q2 2026, and this is a quarterly number. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive, so most of the outflow is capital spending. That one quarter is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025.

## Funding and pipeline
- $3.3B of 7.75% senior secured notes, described in the Q1 2026 results release.
- $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities, reported 14 September 2026.
- Conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data-center sites, reported 14 September 2026. ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions.
- AMD partnership announced 28 July 2026: 500+ MW (megawatts, a unit of power) of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW (gigawatts, 1,000 megawatts).

## Price action and its driver
On 15 October 2026 CORZ rose 7.1% on the day, but it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months and -27.5% over one year. Two retained price points for 7-8 October conflict: one reports a $15.94 price on 2026-10-07 and another reports a close of $18.10 on 2026-10-08. Neither should be used.

The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders, not a CORZ-specific operating failure. On 7-8 October 2026 Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose. Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion. The only company-specific October item found is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05), which is too small to explain the decline.

## Competing forward-looking theses as of 15 October 2026
Bull case: converting low-cost power and land into high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin, and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The assumption to test is that announcements become signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt.

Bear case: a capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow; $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets; negative equity.

Neither side has a clean edge at one week or one month, because direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates. At three months and one year the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating.

# CORZ — Core Scientific, Inc. Common Stock

## Identity
Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) mines bitcoin and rents high-density data-center space. The rental business is called colocation: Core Scientific owns the building and the power supply and rents the space to AI (artificial intelligence) and HPC (high-performance computing) customers. The company exited Chapter 11 in January 2024.

## Merger history (one conflicting date)
CoreWeave agreed to buy Core Scientific in a deal announced on 7 July 2025 (company press release). That deal did not complete. One retained summary says the deal ended in October 2024. That date conflicts with the July 2025 announcement, so treat the termination date as unverified until a filing or press release confirms it. CoreWeave remains the closest listed name for reading sentiment on CORZ.

## Reported results, quarter ended 30 June 2026
- Revenue: $164.2M, up about 109% from $78.6M one year earlier.
- Operating income: +$20.7M. Gross profit: $70.0M, about 43% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA: $41.1M. Liquidity: $1.82B.
- Total assets: $5.26B, up from $3.07B at 31 March 2026. Total liabilities: $7.68B, up from $4.38B.
- Stockholders' equity: -$2.42B at 30 June 2026. Negative book equity means liabilities are larger than assets on the balance sheet. It is not by itself a solvency event.
- Reported net income swung from +$576M in Q1 2025 to -$1.16B in Q2 2026, which points to large non-cash and non-operating items rather than a steady operating loss.

## Cash flow
The free cash flow figure was -$1.02B in Q2 2026, and this is a quarterly number. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new equipment and buildings. Operating cash flow was only -$19.4M and operating income was positive, so most of the outflow is capital spending. That one quarter is more than twice the roughly $459M spent across all four quarters of 2025.

## Funding and pipeline
- $3.3B of 7.75% senior secured notes, described in the Q1 2026 results release.
- $600M of committed senior secured credit facilities, reported 14 September 2026.
- Conditional ERCOT power approvals for Texas data-center sites, reported 14 September 2026. ERCOT is the Texas electric grid operator. Conditional approval means approval with conditions.
- AMD partnership announced 28 July 2026: 500+ MW (megawatts, a unit of power) of U.S. capacity from 2027, stated as scalable to 2.5 GW (gigawatts, 1,000 megawatts).

## Price action and its driver
On 15 October 2026 CORZ rose 7.1% on the day, but it was about -9.3% over one week, -15.6% over one month, -35.4% over three months and -27.5% over one year. Two retained price points for 7-8 October conflict: one reports a $15.94 price on 2026-10-07 and another reports a close of $18.10 on 2026-10-08. Neither should be used.

The multi-month decline tracks a sector-wide repricing of debt-funded data-center builders, not a CORZ-specific operating failure. On 7-8 October 2026 Core Scientific fell about 5% with IREN and TeraWulf as borrowing costs rose. Mid-October pressure returned through the CoreWeave debt debate and hot inflation data that raised the odds of rate rises. The Broadcom CEO warned that financing costs could slow AI expansion. The only company-specific October item found is a small officer sale (Todd Duchene, 10,000 shares, $163,055, sale dated 2026-10-05), which is too small to explain the decline.

## Competing forward-looking theses as of 15 October 2026
Bull case: converting low-cost power and land into high-density AI colocation should raise revenue per megawatt once the halls are leased. Support: revenue more than doubled year over year with a positive gross margin, and the AMD and ERCOT steps are real. The assumption to test is that announcements become signed leases at rents above the cost of the new debt.

Bear case: a capital-intensive builder with negative book equity must keep issuing debt and equity while the build-out consumes cash. A credit squeeze, wider spreads or weaker AI demand expectations raise the funding cost, and the equity absorbs the difference. Support: -$1.02B quarterly free cash flow; $7.68B of liabilities against $5.26B of assets; negative equity.

Neither side has a clean edge at one week or one month, because direction is set by the sector financing narrative and interest rates. At three months and one year the bear case has the firmer current numbers, while the bull case depends on contracts not yet detailed. The bull case is not disproved, because revenue is genuinely accelerating.

## Facts to obtain next
- The CoreWeave deal termination date.
- Contracts for the AMD partnership and other pipeline capacity, with named counterparties, disclosed rent, term and start dates.
- The Q3 2026 report date and results.
- Leasing rents and utilization for the new high-density halls compared with the cost of the new debt.

ticker_packages.answer_markdown: **Bottom line: the facts identify the catalyst and the mechanics clearly, but they do not yet support a directional edge for either side over the next week, month or quarter. The decisive numbers — what Crescent paid per unit of production, how the purchase was funded, and what the combined company earns per share — are not in the evidence.** **What the company is, and what just happened** Crescent Energy Company Class A common stock (ticker CRGY, SEC filer number CIK 1866175) is an independent oil and gas producer with assets in the Permian and Eagle Ford areas. It grows mainly by buying other producers rather than by drilling new ground. It was formed in 2021 by combining Contango Oil & Gas with KKR-backed Independence Energy, and it closed the purchase of Vital Energy's Permian assets on 2025-12-15 for about $3.1 billion including net debt, which the company described as accretive ([CRGY - Crescent Energy Company Class A Common Stock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm)). The current event is the same pattern, larger. On 2026-10-08, Devon Energy agreed to sell its Eagle Ford assets to Crescent for about $4.2 billion in cash, covering roughly 90,000 net acres; one report gives the purchase value as about $3.85 billion and cites roughly $140 million of annual cost savings ([Crescent Energy buys Devon Energy Eagle Ford assets for $4.2B and prices $1B equity offering (October 2026)](https://www.benzinga.com/m/26/10/62241109/devon-energy-sell-its-eagle-ford-assets-crescent-energy-4-2b-cash), [CRGY October 2026 Devon Eagle Ford purchase and Class A stock offering](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRGY/8-k-crescent-energy-company-reports-material-event-0a498471893d.html)). The same day the company started a $1 billion offering of Class A shares. It priced on 2026-10-09 at $12.50 a share for 80 million shares, and a KKR affiliate agreed to buy 40 million of them ([Crescent Energy $1B Class A common stock offering (2026-10-08)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm), [StockTitan: Crescent Energy prices 80M-share stock offering at $12.50](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRGY/8-k-crescent-energy-company-reports-material-event-0a498471893d.html)). One retained record links the offering proceeds to funding the Devon purchase. Another record says the reports do not state the use of proceeds or whether the 80 million shares are new shares, existing shares sold by holders, or a mix. **Reported results before the deal.** For the quarter that ended 2026-06-30, the supplied data show revenue of about $1.39 billion, net income of about $493 million and operating cash flow, the cash a business produces from normal operations, of about $944 million. Total assets were about $12.0 billion, total liabilities about $6.85 billion and shareholders' equity about $5.16 billion. The prior quarter, which ended 2026-03-31, showed a net loss of about $420 million on revenue of about $1.18 billion. The record does not explain what drove the swing between the two quarters. **The bullish hypothesis.** Mechanism: a repeat buyer of oil and gas assets gains scale in the Eagle Ford at a price that is cheaper than building the same production, and the reported cost savings lower the combined unit cost. Supporting facts: the consolidator model has a recent completed example (the Vital Energy Permian purchase, closed 2025-12-15), the $1 billion equity raise removes the need to fund the full cash price from the balance sheet alone, a KKR affiliate committed to half of the offered shares, and second-quarter 2026 results were strongly cash generative. Assumption: the acquisition earns more than its cost of capital and the equity issuance is small relative to the added cash flow. Counterevidence: no purchase agreement terms, no acquired production or reserve figures, no close date and no pro forma financials are in the evidence, so the claim that the deal is accretive cannot be tested. Invalidation: disclosure showing the purchase price per unit of production above comparable regional deals, or pro forma debt that is higher than before the deal without a path to reduce it. **The bearish hypothesis.** Mechanism: the company pays $4.2 billion in cash and sells 80 million new shares at $12.50 to help fund it, so each existing share now represents a smaller slice of the business and more debt. The stock has traded near the offering price since pricing: it closed at $12.84 on 2026-10-14 and fell 2.65% on 2026-10-15 ([CRGY - Crescent Energy Company Class A Common Stock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866175/000119312526419727/d170287d8k.htm)). Supporting facts: the 1-month return is -11.38% and the 1-week return is -7.20% as of 2026-10-15, and the deal report falls inside the 1-week window. Counterevidence: the 3-month return is +20.66%, so the shares are still well above where they started the quarter, and the 1-month window began around 2026-09-14, before the deal was announced, so the deal cannot explain the whole decline. Invalidation: a firm financing plan that holds pro forma debt near current levels, or evidence that per-share cash flow rises after the deal closes. **Which thesis the facts favor.** Neither has a clear edge. The decline is concentrated around a share sale and a large cash purchase, which is consistent with the bearish mechanism, but the same facts are equally consistent with a market that simply repriced the new share count. The bullish mechanism depends on deal economics that are not disclosed. Company identity is confirmed, the catalyst is dated and described, and the pre-deal results are solid on cash generation. Beyond that, the evidence does not settle the question, and guessing would be inventing an edge. **By horizon.** - **1 week:** driven by how the market absorbs the 80 million new shares and whether the stock holds near $12.50. No edge from the evidence. - **1 month:** driven by any further detail on funding, closing conditions and third-quarter results for the period ended 2026-09-30. No edge until those appear. - **3 month:** driven by whether the acquired assets add cash flow per share and whether debt falls. The 3-month return of +20.66% shows the market rewarded the equity earlier in this period, so the pullback is a partial give-back, not a full reversal. **Facts to obtain next.** The purchase agreement: total consideration, cash versus stock, debt financing, expected close date and conditions. The acquired production, reserves and cash flow, so the price can be compared with other Eagle Ford and Permian deals. Pro forma debt, earnings and per-share cash flow, plus share count before and after the offering. Whether the 80 million shares are newly issued. And the driver of the swing from the 2026-03-31 net loss to the 2026-06-30 net profit, including hedging and one-off items.

ticker_packages.answer_markdown: # JetBlue Airways (JBLU) — grounded research brief, 16 October 2026 **Bottom line:** The facts available favour the bearish case for the near horizons (one week to three months), because the last reported quarter shows the loss widening while cash goes out and shareholders' equity shrinks, and because credit raters and analysts have moved the same way. The bullish case depends on a turnaround that has not yet shown up in reported numbers. The next hard fact arrives on 27 October 2026. ## What the company is and what happened to the price JetBlue is a United States passenger airline. It sells seats on domestic routes, to the Caribbean and Latin America, and across the Atlantic. Its profit depends on the money it collects per seat flown one mile against fuel, labour and airport costs. As of 15 October 2026 the shares had risen 4.66% in one day, but they were down 20.8% over one week, 29.2% over one month, 42.3% over three months, 36.5% over one year and 79.8% over five years. Every horizon is marked "Down / worsening". One strong day inside a falling month is not a turn. Two reports describe the slump. On 13 October 2026 the shares fell 4.78% to $3.19, and a Kalkine report linked the fall to a run of negative analyst revisions ([Why did JetBlue sink 4.78% to USD 3.19](https://kalkine.ca/news/travel/why-did-jetblue-airways-nasdaqjblu-sink-478-to-usd-319)). A 14 October 2026 report said the shares fell 7.31% on concern about rising operating costs and weakening demand as banks cut price targets ([JetBlue Airways news, 14 October 2026](https://stockstotrade.com/news/jetblue-airways-corporation-jblu-news-2026_10_14/)). The two reports do not agree on the size of the 14 October move, and neither states the period for its figure. Analyst actions in that window were all negative on price: Susquehanna cut its target to $4 from $6 and kept a Neutral rating, naming unit revenue trends into the fourth quarter as the critical watch point; Goldman Sachs cut to $3.50 from $4 with a Sell rating; TD Cowen stayed at Hold; BMO was named among banks cutting targets. These are analyst target changes, not company forecasts. ## Established business facts Reported quarterly figures to 2026Q2 (period ending 30 June 2026): - Revenue was $2.697bn, up about 14.5% from $2.356bn in 2025Q2. - Net loss was $247m, about three times wider than the $74m loss a year earlier. - Operating loss was $141m. - Free cash flow was negative $318m, and has been negative in every quarter shown from 2024Q4 onward. - Shareholders' equity fell from $2.641bn at 2024Q4 to $1.587bn at 2026Q2, while total liabilities rose to $14.784bn. A 13 October 2026 commentary noted the tension directly: the shares hit fresh 52-week lows even though second-quarter 2026 revenue and unit revenue grew, because losses widened as costs rose. Revenue growing while the loss widens means cost growth is running ahead of pricing. On credit, S&P Global Ratings lowered JetBlue to CCC+ from B- on 8 June 2026 with a stable outlook, citing elevated fuel costs and sustained high leverage ([JetBlue Financials: Losses, Debt & JetForward Turnaround](https://dwuconsulting.com/dwu-ai/jetblue-airways-financial-profile)). CCC+ is a rating grade that signals substantial credit risk. A separate CreditSights note frames cash burn and Middle East tensions as the drivers of liquidity concern, with financing options drawing focus ([JetBlue cash burn, Middle East tensions fuel liquidity concerns](https://know.creditsights.com/insights/us-special-situations-jetblue-cash-burn-middle-east-tensions-fuel-liquidity-concerns-as-financing-options-draw-focus/)). ## Bearish hypothesis **Mechanism:** Fuel, labour and airport costs rise faster than the money collected per seat mile. Revenue per seat grows, but the loss widens anyway, so the company keeps spending more cash than it earns. Falling equity and high leverage then make borrowing more expensive or force a share sale, which spreads the same profit over more shares. **Supporting facts:** Q2 2026 revenue up 14.5% but the loss about three times wider; negative free cash flow in every quarter shown; equity down about 40% from 2024Q4; the S&P downgrade to CCC+; negative analyst target revisions into 14 October 2026. **Assumption:** The cost trend of the last reported quarter continues into the third quarter. **Counterevidence:** Susquehanna kept a Neutral rating rather than Sell, and the 13 October commentary described the situation as a contrarian setup. Revenue and unit revenue did grow. **Observable invalidation:** The Q3 2026 report shows a narrower loss and unit revenue growth above unit cost growth; or no new financing is needed on expensive terms; or a credit rater lifts the outlook. ## Bullish hypothesis **Mechanism:** The JetForward turnaround pushes revenue up faster than costs. Higher revenue per seat then converts into a smaller loss rather than a wider one, and a stock near its 52-week low with a Sell rating already priced in re-rates when the loss narrows. **Supporting facts:** Revenue rose 14.5% year on year in 2026Q2 and unit revenue grew; the shares bounced 4.66% on 15 October 2026. **Assumption:** Fuel prices fall or capacity is cut enough that cost growth slows below revenue growth. **Counterevidence:** The loss widened in the same quarter that revenue grew, which is the opposite of the mechanism. Goldman Sachs carries a Sell rating, and S&P rates the debt CCC+. One up day inside a 42% three-month fall does not show a change in the business. **Observable invalidation:** The Q3 2026 report shows a further widening loss, or a new share issue or expensive borrowing, or another credit downgrade. ## Which thesis the facts favour The bearish thesis has the better support on the facts in hand, because the only reported quarter shows costs outrunning pricing while cash leaves the business, and because the credit and analyst moves point the same way. That is an edge on the reported trajectory, not a forecast. The bullish case rests on a turnaround that has not yet appeared in any reported number, so it is a claim about the future rather than a reading of the evidence. The edge is strongest over one week to three months and weakest over one year to five years, where the outcome depends on whether the turnaround ever produces positive free cash flow. That question is unresolved. ## Facts to obtain next - The third-quarter 2026 results, due on the call at 10:00 a.m. ET on 27 October 2026 (JetBlue Announces Webcast of Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call, 13 October 2026). Unit revenue against unit cost is the decisive comparison. - The company's stated full-year 2026 guidance and any capacity or route changes. - Total liquidity and the maturity schedule for the next twelve months, to test how far cash burn can continue without new funding. - The fuel hedge position and the current share count. - Whether the 13 and 14 October 2026 price falls had a company-specific trigger beyond the analyst revisions. This is research, not a recommendation to buy or sell.
